prompt: For a materially different sanitized infrastructure change supplied by a qualified reviewer, produce and defend a complete IaC change-system design, plan review, partial-failure recovery and post-change verification. Do not use lesson fixtures or model answers, and do not initialize a provider, use credentials or change infrastructure without separate explicit authorization.
deliverables: Managed-system boundary, user objective, resource owners, alternate controllers and explicit exclusions.
Exact configuration revision, variable source, CLI, provider, module, dependency lock, policy and test identities.
Target identity covering account/project/subscription, tenant, region, principal, backend, workspace, state lineage and serial.
Desired configuration, state binding and remote-observation comparison with one-to-one ownership checks.
Dependency graph with implicit/explicit edges, unknowns, parallelism, cycles, readiness and destruction order.
Plan review naming every create, update, replace, delete, import, forget and no-op plus consequence and owner.
Drift classification with actor/source, urgency, authorization and adopt/revert/ownership-transfer decision.
State design covering locking, concurrency, encryption, access, versioning, audit, snapshots, restore and break-glass operations.
Pipeline trust design covering protected source, runner isolation, supply chain, short-lived least privilege, plan/apply separation, policy, exceptions and approval.
Partial-failure timeline with remote/state ambiguity, evidence preservation, supported reconciliation and fresh-plan path.
Staged execution with communication, abort, rollback or roll-forward, quota, capacity, data, security and cost boundaries.
Post-change provider, state, user, data, security, observability, capacity and cost verification plus full convergence plan.
evidenceRequirements: Sanitized inputs with provenance, timestamp, versions, target population and known gaps.
Graph and action inventory that can be independently recalculated from the supplied case.
Exact plan or fictional equivalent bound to source, state and target digests; screenshots alone are insufficient.
At least one replacement or deletion challenged through data, identity, availability and recovery consequences.
One drift case where automatic revert is unsafe and the ownership decision is defended.
One partial or ambiguous execution case resolved without deleting state or assuming transaction rollback.
Reviewer-observed proof that no provider, credential, remote backend, paid resource or real infrastructure was used.
Delayed reassessment on a second unseen system with different ownership and failure semantics.

rubric.observableEvidence: Defines managed scope, owners, objectives, alternate controllers and exclusions.
Pins source, dependencies, variables, policy, backend, state, target and principal.
Explains binding, lineage, locking, sensitivity, versioning and recovery.
Explains edges, unknowns, parallelism, cycles, readiness and destruction.
Names every action and consequence, especially replacements and deletions.
Classifies source, authorization, urgency and adopt/revert/transfer path.
Covers supply chain, credentials, artifacts, state, policy, exceptions and duties.
Preserves evidence, resolves ambiguity and creates a fresh complete plan.
Stages change with approval, communication, abort and rollback/roll-forward.
Checks provider, state, users, data, security, capacity, cost and convergence.
Compares module, state, environment and automation alternatives.
States decision, evidence, uncertainty, owner, limits and review trigger.
